summary: The 2026 Iran war (the US and Israel against Iran, since Feb 28) has heated up again after a tense pause: UKMTO reported tankers attacked north of Oman's Khasab on Nov 17 and Nov 20, and a US military official told Reuters that US aircraft struck an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island on Nov 17. On Saturday, Nov 21, UKMTO reported two tanker incidents near Khasab (a projectile hit on one tanker's stern and another in a tanker's engine room, possibly the same vessel), and Iran's navy said a tanker caught fire after hitting a mine east of the strait. Bahrain said two people were injured in an Iranian strike on a civilian industrial site on Nov 21, while Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted US bases there. Iran's deputy foreign minister said a Qatari delegation held two hours of talks in Tehran on Nov 20 (AFP, Iran International). On Nov 22 the tracking firm TankerTrackers said ship-tracking signals showing an Iranian tanker, the Khat-Shekan, sailing through the strait toward the US blockade were a spoof and that the vessel does not exist (Euronews). On Sunday evening UKMTO reported a tanker incident involving military forces in the Gulf of Oman near Chabahar, with investigations ongoing (Euronews). Iran's foreign minister said talks must be given a chance; no agreement has been announced.

status.label: Strait of Hormuz
status.note: Iran says it is closed to ships that don't coordinate with its Persian Gulf Strait Authority; the US says the main routes are controlled by the US and its regional partners. Most traffic moves through a shuttle system the US coordinates with Arab partners, with weekly volumes swinging as attacks continue (Al Jazeera).

status.label: Oil through Hormuz
status.note: About 11.6 million barrels a day over the seven days to Oct 13, about 68% of the 17.1 million pre-war baseline (Kpler, via Al Jazeera). This is the latest weekly figure found; no newer one had been confirmed by Nov 18.

status.label: The war
status.note: A US military official told Reuters that US fighter aircraft struck an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island on Nov 17, after earlier limited US strikes there on Nov 2 and Nov 7 and on launchers at Bandar Lengeh and Sirik over Nov 15-16 (Euronews). On Nov 17 Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted a US radar system in Bahrain with drones; Bahrain said it intercepted the attacks. Qatar, a mediator, called for restraint; no deal has been signed. On Nov 21 Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they struck US bases in Bahrain; Bahrain said an Iranian strike on a civilian industrial site injured two people (AFP). A Qatari delegation held two hours of talks in Tehran on Nov 20, Iran's deputy foreign minister said (AFP).

status.label: Brent crude
status.note: Brent settled at US$92.57 a barrel on Friday, Nov 20 (WTI US$83.98 for the expiring December contract, US$83.41 for the most-active January one), after falling to about US$90 earlier in the day; oil posted a third straight weekly decline (EnergyNow; Bloomberg via Rigzone).

updates.text: At his weekly briefing on Monday, Nov 23, Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei called the US naval blockade an act of military aggression and said Iran would use every means to counter it; he said security in the strait could be restored quickly if the US lifted sanctions and the blockade and met the June memorandum's terms.
sources: Euronews: Iran vows 'every means' to counter US blockade of Hormuz after Trump threat

updates.text: Asked on Sunday, Nov 22, about Iranian ships trying to break the blockade, President Trump told a Fox News reporter they would "all go down to the bottom of the sea" if they tried; Tasnim said no official Iranian convoy plan had been announced.
sources: Euronews: Iran vows 'every means' to counter US blockade of Hormuz after Trump threat

updates.text: CNN reported on Sunday, Nov 22, that Iranian attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz had reached their highest level since the war began; OilPrice.com also reported stepped-up tanker attacks as oil prices slid.
sources: CNN: Iranian attacks in the Strait of Hormuz are at the highest levels since the conflict began
OilPrice.com: Iran Steps Up Hormuz Tanker Attacks as Oil Prices Slide

updates.text: UKMTO said a tanker was involved in an incident with military forces in the Gulf of Oman, east of the Strait of Hormuz near Iran's Chabahar; it said authorities are aware and investigations are ongoing. No damage or injuries were reported and no party has commented (Euronews).
sources: Euronews: Tanker incident involving military forces reported in Strait of Hormuz

updates.text: Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry condemned Saturday's Iranian attack on an industrial facility in Bahrain and said Iran would bear the consequences if such attacks continued (Iran International, citing the ministry).
sources: Iran International live: Saudi Arabia warns Iran of consequences after attack on Bahrain injures two

updates.text: The tracking firm TankerTrackers said on Sunday, Nov 22, that ship-tracking signals showing an Iranian tanker called the Khat-Shekan ("line-breaker") sailing through the Strait of Hormuz were a spoof and that the vessel does not exist; satellite images did not match the signals (Euronews). Iran's deputy foreign minister said a Qatari delegation held two hours of talks in Tehran on Friday evening, Nov 20 (AFP, Iran International).
sources: Euronews: Tracking site says Iranian tanker reportedly sailing through Strait of Hormuz does not exist
Prothom Alo (AFP): Tankers struck in Hormuz, as Iran says held talks with mediator Qatar
Iran International: 'Line-breaker' tanker signal near Hormuz was fake

updates.text: Bahrain's interior ministry said on Sunday, Nov 22, that two people were injured in Saturday's Iranian strike on a civilian industrial facility, which caused a fire and damage: a Bahraini citizen in stable condition and a Pakistani resident in critical condition (AFP via Arab News). On Saturday the ministry had reported no casualties.
sources: Arab News (AFP): Bahrain says two injured in Iranian attack on industrial site

updates.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they hit US positions at the Al-Riffa and Awali bases in Bahrain with missiles and drones on Saturday, Nov 21; Bahrain's Defence Force said its air defences intercepted several attacks and that falling debris caused material damage.

UKMTO reported a second incident on Saturday, Nov 21: a tanker hit in its engine room by an unidentified projectile 17 nautical miles east of Khasab; it was not clear whether both reports involved the same vessel, and no casualties were reported. Iran's navy said a tanker caught fire after hitting a naval mine in a restricted area east of the strait; Reuters could not verify the Iranian account.
sources: Reuters via ThePrint: UK maritime agency reports two tanker incidents near Oman; Iran says vessel hit mine east of Hormuz
Jerusalem Post: Two tankers hit by unidentified projectiles in Strait of Hormuz off Oman's Khasab within an hour

background: The war began on Feb 28, 2026 with US and Israeli strikes on Iran. An April ceasefire collapsed on July 8. The US has blockaded Iranian ports since April (reinstated in July); Iran restricts and attacks shipping through Hormuz, which carried about a fifth of the world's oil before the war.
factcheck: Checked by Claude against at least two reputable sources where possible. Statements by Iran's military, the US military (CENTCOM) or President Trump are labelled as claims, because each side's account of who controls the strait differs.
